scope: Independent near-view experiment, not a replacement for the 2382-triangle base asset.
visible_improvement: Main boughs lead into tapering secondary branchlet fans and fine terminal woody shoots; junction hierarchy is visible in both hero directions.
Short narrow solid needle groups replace the broad spear-like leaf blocks of the baseline.
Unequal bough lengths, varying shoot scale and open gaps avoid a stack of matching cones.

iteration.observed_defect: The first rendered sample had needle envelopes too narrow to read at the intended medium viewing scale; crown looked skeletal.
iteration.correction: Widened and lengthened the existing needle-bundle envelopes, especially on lower and middle shoots. No extra triangles were added for this correction.

tradeoffs: 14118 triangles is 5.93 times the baseline; 36144 exported POSITION vertices is 7.32 times the baseline.
The crown remains intentionally open and spiky. Fine foliage is less robust at thumbnail/distant scale than the baseline large masses.
At 128px overall tree silhouette is visible, but individual needle groups largely disappear. Preferred object coverage is 350–650px.
No Three.js runtime performance benchmark or user aesthetic approval is claimed.
No compliance with RHS059/low_poly_items vertex limits is claimed.
comparison_controls: Same union-bounds camera framing, key/fill lighting, Standard view transform, 1024px and 32 samples. Shared preview fixtures are absent from both exported assets.
conclusion: Branch and foliage identity improves at close-to-medium range, at a substantial geometry cost. Retain the original base asset as default; this sample is for an explicit visual-versus-cost decision only.
